pr_body:
closes #216

This PR provides defaults for title/body in a PR based on commits.

If 1 commit: PR title is commit message, body is commit body
If >1 commits: PR title is branch, body is listing of commits

Note that in both cases, PR templates supersede the body generation.

## Test suite changes

This PR also adds two improvements to our test suite:

- `AskStubber`. This can be used to simulate user input to a prompt created by `survey`. You can either specify specific values that a user would input or just have  `survey` use the default. 
- `CmdStubber`. This allows us to set up a number of expected calls to external commands. It's pretty simple for now and is intended to just replace the hacky ExecStubber thing that was there previously and add the ability to stub multiple times (instead of a single call to `SetPrepareCmd`.

I didn't add any new test coverage beside the coverage for computing PR defaults but we can now exercise more code paths than we could previously as we had no utility for stubbing `survey.Ask`.

## Demo gif

![defaults](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/98482/76657197-47319c00-653f-11ea-9a45-9f7244d7ecd8.gif)

issue_context.title: Autofill PR title and body with commit message and body
issue_context.body:
"I usually use the commit message + commit body to auto-fill PR titles (for single-commit PRs) and descriptions on GitHub, but this tool asked me for that info outside of those, so it was either retype or just cancel and create it on the browser."
 
"I really enjoy how hub auto-populates a Pull Request title and body with the branches last commit, if it is the only committed change. I wish the gh CLI would do that as well."

- From feedback form
comments: I assume this is just for PRs with single commits? I'm trying to imagine the implications of this and how it might work on CLI. Do you just get to say, "here's the PR with the auto-filled fields, do you want this?" with yes/no and then if you say no you can manually do the `gh pr create` as normal?

Yes only for single commits! 

In my head, I was expecting:

1. For title, we'd autopopulate the title in gray. You'd hit enter to accept it, or start typing to override it
2. For body, the description would prefill in the editor (overriding the template?) where you can delete it if you want

Is this doable? Would others expect other flows?

Having the title autocomplete for PRs with >1 commit would be helpful too, it's something I use in the web version all the time.

Edit: Just to clarify, the web version uses the branch name as the default PR title, which is what I'm suggesting the `gh` CLI do as well.

Personally, I would prefer the `git commit` model, where I'm dumped in `$EDITOR` and `gh` would parse the temporary file to extract necessary info. I find the wizard too slow. `$EDITOR` is ingrained in my muscles.

#340 asks to support different fields, such as assignee and reviewer, label, etc. `gh` could offer YAML documents to support such a use case:

```yaml
Reviewer: # leave blank to not fill in
Labels: # leave blank to not fill in
---
PR TITLE

PR BODY
```

`PR TITLE` and `BODY` could be pre-filled with the first commit on the branch.

I would prefer a text editor as well.

Automatically filling in a single commit's title and body works well; for multiple commits, consider leaving the title blank but providing a commented-out summary of the commits that people can then use to summarize their PR.

Support for $EDITOR would be great - keeping it consistent with git commit feels natural.

YAML front matter for additional fields is a nice idea, but I'm more apt to edit those on the web where I have auto complete.

some actions items for now (which might warrant a new issue):

- auto fill survey prompts (including body) for single commit PRs
- add a flag (maybe `-f`/`--fill`) to autofill and submit with zero prompts
On web, "filling" is the default, right? Maybe it could do it by default if there is only one commit? I've been working around this by just using `-w` to get the default behavior there.

What I've discovered is that at least for single-commit PRs if I just hit Enter at the "Title?" prompt without filling anything, it does construct the title from the commit, at least if I then do Preview In Browser (I haven't yet tried just creating it directly). But I don't know what it does with multiple commits, and I'd really like it to tell me what the title will be if I don't fill one in.

review_comments: Something that I've learned in hub is that we should try to pre-emptively negate the `log.showSignature` setting, otherwise based on the user's settings the `git log` command might try to calculate the validity of signed commits. https://github.com/github/hub/commit/910dfdcb500dd7866939ed65bd5d37d7d42e3356
Good thinking. I'm definitely up for extracting parts of utils into isolated packages, or even interface-only packages 👍
cool--i definitely felt a desire for interface-only packages while working on this stuff.

I love the command stubber! One idea: instead of denoting the expected command in code comments, how about we enforce it in the expectation itself?

```suggestion
	cs.Stub("git status", "")
	cs.Stub("git log", "1234567890,commit 0\n2345678901,commit 1")
	cs.Stub("git push", "")
```

I think it would make for more resilient tests in the long run. I'm not sure how easy would it be to make it "match", though.
this is a direction i thought we might go if you liked the `CmdStubber`. I'd love to add this; would you be ok with it being a follow-up?
